reason: Phenotype is dominated by craniofacial/ear anomalies with several fairly specific features (lower eyelid coloboma, absent eyelashes, external auditory canal atresia, micrognathia, malar flattening). This should allow PCF to rank strongly, but overlap across multiple syndromes argues for retaining a moderate PCF set. Facial gestalt appears distinctive and image-based tools can add complementary capture of syndromes where facial pattern drives ranking; however, image uncertainty and potential noise favor a smaller yet nontrivial GestaltMatcher cut. Asymmetric allocation (more to PCF than GM) balances higher expected precision from explicit HPO specificity with added coverage from facial similarity while keeping total review cost <=20.
